one_liner: Experienced DOJ litigator who tracks down, seizes, and forfeits assets from fraudsters and collects court judgments for the United States in federal court.
fit_summary: This job requires a J.D., an active bar license and at least 2.5 years of post-J.D. legal experience including litigation. Daniel's degree is an M.A. in Global Affairs, so he does not qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens), so no federal status is needed.
Requires a J.D. or equivalent from an accredited school, plus active bar membership in good standing in any U.S. state, territory, or DC.

GS-14 requires 2.5 years of post-J.D. legal experience, including 1 year of specialized experience at GS-13 level, such as drafting pleadings or conducting civil or criminal litigation. GS-15 requires 4 years, including 1 year at GS-14 level.
Requires the ability to obtain a Secret security clearance.
keywords: pleadings, briefs, and other court documents
strategy: Skip this one: HR screens out applicants without a J.D. and bar license.

Target related non-attorney roles instead, such as FEMA or DOJ grant and program analyst jobs, Virginia Department of Emergency Management positions, Prince William County emergency management, or legislative aide roles that fit his policy knowledge.
interview_questions: Describe a case where you traced and recovered assets or enforced a judgment. What tools did you use?
How do you coordinate with law enforcement and criminal prosecutors while handling a parallel civil enforcement action?
Walk us through how you would handle a contested writ of garnishment in federal court.
Tell us about a time you advised senior managers on a complex legal issue.
watch_outs: A J.D. and active bar license are mandatory, and he has neither.
The job requires a Secret clearance and up to 7% travel.
The long open period does not change the J.D. and active bar membership requirement.
